people.name: Al Orsatti
people.note: Agency partner with Frank, Vic and Ernie; his clients included actress Peggy O'Neill. Died by 1949 of a heart attack, aged 48 (Weaver et al.). Likely father of SAG leader Ken (Alfred Kendall) Orsatti – inferred.

people.name: Victor "Vic" Orsatti
people.note: Ernie's brother: USC quarterback, agent to Judy Garland and Sonja Henie, later a producer. Formed Sabre Productions on Sept 17, 1953, planning This Island Earth as its first film (the picture was made at Universal). Producer credits: Flight to Hong Kong (assoc., 1956), Ride Out for Revenge (assoc., 1957), Domino Kid and The Hired Gun (1957), Apache Territory (1958), A Face in the Rain (exec., 1963), plus the CBS western The Texan (1958–60) with Rory Calhoun. Earliest credit: script clerk on Spring Fever (1927).

people.name: Ernie Orsatti
people.note: Keaton prop man/stuntman, Cardinals outfielder, agent.

people.name: Frank Orsatti (agent)
people.note: Founded the Orsatti Agency in 1930 after a career described as bootlegging; reputed fixer for MGM's Louis B. Mayer; agent to Judy Garland. Died by 1949 of a heart attack, aged 53 (Weaver et al.). Not the same person as Frank H. Orsatti the stuntman.

people.name: Ernie F. Orsatti ("Earnest")
people.note: Ernest Frank Orsatti, born Beverly Hills Feb 13, 1940; died La Quinta Sept 12, 2020. Nicknamed "The Legend." Mother: opera singer Inez Gorman. A Foster Grant model and swimmer trained under Johnny Weissmuller; three Death Wish films, Hot Shots!, Alien: Resurrection, American History X, NYPD Blue, Charmed.

people.name: Frank H. Orsatti (stuntman)
people.note: Ernie's son; doubled Schwarzenegger, Burt Reynolds, Bill Bixby.

people.name: Noon Orsatti
people.note: Son of Ernie F.; stunt coordinator / 2nd-unit director. Won the 2024 Taurus World Stunt Award (Extraction 2); in the SAG Awards stunt-ensemble nominees for The Falcon and the Winter Soldier (2022). Chad Stahelski recalls working for Ernie F. and Noon on NYPD Blue, The Pretender and Profiler – and that Noon sent him to the Matrix audition.

people.name: Ken Orsatti (Alfred Kendall)
people.note: Nephew of Ernie: his father and two uncles ran the Orsatti Agency (LA Times). Rorvic Productions assistant 1956; SAG national executive director 1981–2000.

milestones.title: Stunts Unlimited
milestones.text: Frank H. Orsatti was one of the original members of Stunts Unlimited, the elite stunt association co-founded by Hal Needham, Ronnie Rondell and Glenn Wilder. In 2019 the group named him an honorary member. He started in stunts in 1968 on Planet of the Apes, jumped off the Golden Gate Bridge for B.S. I Love You, doubled Burt Reynolds for nine years, and directed twelve episodes of The Incredible Hulk.
milestones.flag: Founding year 1970 per Stunts Unlimited history; Frank described as an original member

milestones.title: "Frank Orsatti created a stunt legacy."
milestones.text: "…he gave so many second unit directors and stunt coordinators their first breaks as stunt performers, myself included." – Manny Perry, Stunts Unlimited, on being hired by Frank to double Lou Ferrigno on The Incredible Hulk.

milestones.title: Rowbie Orsatti's first credit: Charmed
milestones.text: Rowbie Orsatti's first screen credit came on Charmed in 1998, a show the family ran for years: his grandfather Ernie F. Orsatti was its stunt coordinator (37 episodes), and his father Noon Orsatti also worked on the series.

milestones.title: Rowbie Orsatti joins SAG
milestones.text: Rowbie Orsatti becomes a member of the Screen Actors Guild – the union Ken Orsatti led as national executive director from 1981 to 2000.

milestones.title: The Orsatti TV years
milestones.text: Through the late 1990s and 2000s Ernie F. and Noon Orsatti coordinated stunts across a remarkable run of network and cable series – Charmed, Carnivàle, Entourage, It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia, Nip/Tuck, The Closer, Big Love and more. The family recalls a stretch when father and son were running more shows than anyone in town.

milestones.title: Bootleggers to the studios
milestones.text: Family lore holds that the Orsatti brothers supplied Hollywood – and MGM in particular – during Prohibition. The documented pieces: author Tim Adler says Frank got into the movie business by supplying Louis B. Mayer with alcohol and women; Weaver et al. call Frank "a former bootlegger"; and father Morris was convicted (1922–25) of bribing a Prohibition agent.
sources: Tom Weaver, David Schecter & Robert J. Kiss, Universal Terrors, 1951–1955 (McFarland, 2017)

milestones.title: Vic's spaghetti parties
milestones.text: A period news photo shows Al and Victor Orsatti with Alice Faye, James Stewart, Rochelle Hudson and Shirley Ross at "one of Victor Orsatti's famous Hollywood spaghetti parties."

milestones.title: Bringing Sonja Henie to Hollywood
milestones.text: Vic is credited with persuading three-time Olympic figure-skating champion Sonja Henie to move to Hollywood after the 1936 Winter Olympics; she became one of its highest-paid stars. In 1939 Louella Parsons reported their romance was "the talk of Hollywood."

milestones.title: Ernest Ralph Orsatti is born
milestones.text: Born Sept 8, 1902 in Los Angeles, sixth of seven children of Italian immigrants Maurizio and Maria (Manze) Orsatti – anglicized to Morris and Mary. Morris had been a tailor in Philadelphia; in Los Angeles he owned the International Steamship and Railroad Ticket Agency.
milestones.flag: Emigration date, ship and Italian hometown not found

milestones.title: Quitting school for the movies
milestones.text: "My interest, as a boy, was in motion pictures and not in baseball… In 1920, I decided to quit school and devote all my time to the picture business." He worked as a gofer, then a stuntman: wing-walking, cliff dives, car and boat stunts. From 1922 he was Keaton's prop man and bit player, and played first base and catcher on Keaton's team (1922–25).

milestones.title: Morris Orsatti and the Prohibition agent
milestones.text: A federal indictment charged Morris Orsatti with promising and paying bribes to Prohibition agent Harold H. Dolley (from June 1922) to drop or reduce cases against arrested liquor-law violators. Convicted on all 21 counts; the Ninth Circuit affirmed in Orsatti v. United States, 3 F.2d 778 (Feb 2, 1925), and the Supreme Court denied review on May 4, 1925.
milestones.flag: Court record; identity with the patriarch is strongly implied (Los Angeles, same name) but not stated in the opinion

milestones.title: Babe Ruth's bat
milestones.text: Ernie's brother Vic, named best all-around high-school athlete in Los Angeles, won the bat Babe Ruth used for the first home run at Yankee Stadium (April 18, 1923) in a Los Angeles Evening Herald home-run contest. It sold in 2004 for about $1.26 million.

milestones.title: Climbing the Cardinals farm
milestones.text: Branch Rickey bought his contract after seeing him hit .347 at Cedar Rapids (1925). He hit .386 at Omaha in 1926 and .330 at Houston in 1927, then .381 with 15 HR at Minneapolis in 1928. On Aug 24, 1928 his first-inning homer beat the Phillies 1–0 and kept St. Louis in first place.

milestones.title: Best season: .336 – and Rickey's phone trick
milestones.text: Ernie hit .336 (sixth in the NL). When he asked Branch Rickey for a raise over $4,500, Rickey took two "calls" from farm clubs asking for an outfielder; Ernie asked only for a pen to sign. Bill Veeck Sr. later said the calls were fake, rung by a foot pedal under Rickey's desk.

milestones.title: "Orsatti was a showman."
milestones.text: Teammate Jim Mooney recalled him catching a line drive and turning "two or three somersaults." In the 1934 World Series he played all seven games, hitting .318. Detroit fans were still bitter 25 years later: Frankie Frisch said a Detroit hotel clerk refused Ernie a room.

milestones.title: Orsatti Bail Bonds
milestones.text: Ernie married Alice Joyce Ritchie in 1960 and ran Orsatti Bail Bonds in Van Nuys with her until his death on Sept 4, 1968. He is buried at San Fernando Mission Cemetery. His son Ernie F. remembered him as a great athlete and a talented chef who cooked Christmas Eve dinner for dozens of show-business and opera guests.

milestones.title: Frank H. tries the family game
milestones.text: Ernie's son Frank played 12 games for the Cardinals' affiliate Brunswick (Georgia-Florida League) in 1963 before an injury ended his career; he later spent ten years in the Merchant Marine before becoming a stuntman.

milestones.title: The Orsatti family begins in Hollywood
milestones.text: 1923 is the founding year on the family's own crest (est. 1923); Noon Orsatti's IMDb bio also says the Orsatti name has been synonymous with film making since 1923.
milestones.flag: Per family logo; no independent record found

milestones.title: Fired… into pro baseball
milestones.text: Per Keaton biographer James Curtis, Ernie "was so good that one day in 1925 he arrived at work and found a new set of luggage and a check…and was told he was fired. Keaton handed him a contract to play for the Vernon Tigers."
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernie_Orsatti (citing Curtis, Buster Keaton: A Filmmaker's Life, 2022, p.280)

milestones.title: MLB debut – St. Louis Cardinals
milestones.text: Ernie debuts September 4, 1927. Career 1927–35: 701 games, .306 average, 663 hits, 10 HR, 237 RBI. Bats and throws left.

milestones.title: World Series champion
milestones.text: Ernie played in four World Series (1928, 1930, 1931, 1934), winning in 1931 and 1934; .273 across 13 Series games.

milestones.title: "The envy of most of the younger players"
milestones.text: "His flashy sweaters, golf hose, knickers and sports suits are Hollywood importations, and his wardrobe is the envy of most of the younger players." – The Sporting News, 1932. SABR: "Ernie's ensembles made him stand out like a peacock in the ranks of the Gashouse Gang."

milestones.title: Gashouse Gang – 1934 champions
milestones.text: Ernie was part of the famously scruffy 1934 "Gashouse Gang" Cardinals who won the World Series; he drove in both of his career Series RBIs that fall.

milestones.title: Frank Orsatti opens the Orsatti Agency
milestones.text: "In 1930, their son Frank, a former bootlegger, went into the agency business and brought in his brothers Al, Victor and Ernie. The Orsatti Agency represented actors, executives, producers, directors, writers and radio talent." The same book says father Morris Orsatti, a bank vice-president, had ties to organized crime and "spent time up the river in the 1920s."
sources: Tom Weaver, David Schecter & Robert J. Kiss, Universal Terrors, 1951–1955 (McFarland, 2017), This Island Earth chapter
milestones.flag: Single published source; father's prison term not independently verified

milestones.title: Victor takes charge
milestones.text: "By 1949 Frank and Al were dead of heart attacks (at 53 and 48, respectively) and Victor took charge."
sources: Tom Weaver, David Schecter & Robert J. Kiss, Universal Terrors, 1951–1955 (McFarland, 2017), This Island Earth chapter

milestones.title: The Orsatti Talent Agency
milestones.text: After his last MLB game (Sept 28, 1935) Ernie joins brothers Frank, Vic and Al in the Orsatti Talent Agency. Clients included Judy Garland, Sonja Henie, Betty Grable, Edward G. Robinson, Margaret O'Brien, Alice Faye, Frank Capra and George Stevens. His son called it the largest agency in Hollywood.

milestones.title: Frank Orsatti & the Wizard of Oz
milestones.text: Agent Frank Orsatti told MGM producer Arthur Freed that Samuel Goldwyn held the rights to The Wizard of Oz – the film that made Orsatti client Judy Garland a legend. Vic Orsatti negotiated her Dorothy contract.

milestones.title: "Handling all of MGM's dirty work"
milestones.text: Author Tim Adler (Hollywood and the Mob, 2011) called Frank Orsatti "a bootlegger and gangster" who got into the movie business by supplying Louis B. Mayer with alcohol and women, with a reputation for "handling all of MGM's 'dirty work'." Adler called Vic a "gangster-cum-agent." Allegations from one author, not court findings.

milestones.title: One last season
milestones.text: Ernie returns for 1939 with the Hollywood Stars (PCL) and Columbus. The New York Times said Orsatti, "now an actors' agent, is expected to prove a strong drawing card in the film colony."

milestones.title: "Husbands are much easier to find than good agents."
milestones.text: Actress Marie "The Body" McDonald (married to Vic Orsatti 1943–47, formerly Bugsy Siegel's girlfriend) kept him as her agent after the divorce.

milestones.title: The Bugsy Siegel connection
milestones.text: Vic Orsatti's wife Marie McDonald had previously been Bugsy Siegel's girlfriend (Wikipedia, citing Tim Adler). A fan-history site further claims that during her 1947 Las Vegas divorce stay from Orsatti she rode the Flamingo Hotel float for Siegel – that detail is from a non-scholarly source.

milestones.title: Ernie Orsatti's Oddity Shop and Florist
milestones.text: In the mid-1940s Ernie opened an oddity shop and florist on Sunset Boulevard (with his brothers-in-law, per Wikipedia). Business cards: Cardinals redbirds perched on a bat. He also held a patent on a candy-vending machine, collecting royalties on candy sold in most Southern California theater lobbies.

milestones.title: "Third from the top"
milestones.text: The St. Louis Star and Times (Oct 1, 1946) said the Orsatti agency was "third from the top where movie actors' agents get together."

milestones.title: Saber Productions & Rorvic Productions
milestones.text: Vic Orsatti's Saber Productions produced films incl. Flight to Hong Kong (1956); Rorvic Productions (with Rory Calhoun) made CBS's The Texan.

milestones.title: Ken Orsatti: SAG National Executive Director
milestones.text: Ken Orsatti (1932–2010), SAG national executive director 1981–2000, negotiated ~20 major contracts and helped found the SAG Foundation. Sources call him national executive director (the Guild's top staff executive and chief negotiator), not SAG president (an elected actor post). Born Alfred Kendall Orsatti; his father and two uncles ran the Orsatti Agency, so he was Ernie's nephew (most likely Al's son).
milestones.flag: Which brother was his father is inferred from his name (Alfred)

milestones.title: Ken Orsatti joins SAG
milestones.text: Ken Orsatti starts at the Screen Actors Guild as a theatrical business rep; Southwest regional director 1966; Hollywood exec director 1971–81.

milestones.title: Taurus World Stunt Award
milestones.text: Noon Orsatti wins the Taurus World Stunt Award for Best Stunt Coordinator and/or 2nd Unit Director for Extraction 2 – the third generation of the family in film.
